run.what: the commit this batch was generated on; 'local' means it was run by hand rather than by CI

model.name: Z-Image-Turbo
model.licence_note: Apache-2.0 model weights; outputs unrestricted. No account, no terms to accept, no purchase.

content_rules: invented fictional shop name only, no real company names, no real brand logos, no trade marks, no real person, no recognisable faces, no celebrity likeness
rights: Model weights Apache-2.0; outputs unrestricted by the model licence. No third-party asset was an input. Prompts name only in-world Meridian businesses. NOTHING SHIPS UNREVIEWED: every image below is review=pending until a human has looked for anything resembling a real mark or a real face.
caps: --limit: at most 4 picture(s) GENERATED this run; items already on disk that pass the skip check do not count against it

blank_check.what: every written PNG is decoded and its luminance measured; a uniform image is the known Vulkan failure (leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp#1031: blank PNG, exit success)
blank_check.bound: blank when spread <= 2/255 AND stdev <= 1.0, or alpha is 0 everywhere sampled

resume.what: recipe = prompt + negative(if it can act) + size + cfg + steps + seed; a match is skipped, a mismatch is made again
resume.record: nothing on record; 0 item(s) on record in total

negatives.what: --negative-prompt is passed whenever an item has one; it only ACTS when cfg != 1.0, because sd-cli evaluates the unconditional branch only then

selection.what: only = the ids asked for by name; limit = how many pictures this run may GENERATE, which skipped items do not count against

images.binds_to: CONCEPT SHEET - reviewed by eye, bound to no mesh, no material and no bill-of-materials row. Fairview, the second of seven district sheets drawn by this lane, and the first whose prompt was authored from this project's own sources. Jafar 2026-09-10.
images.prompt: one printed sheet filling the frame edge to edge, A concept sheet for FAIRVIEW, the residential hills of Meridian, a fictional British port town, in 1990. Two stacked photoreal panels inside a pale paper border: top an orientation view, bottom the same district at standing eye height. TOP: from the crest road at 40 m, looking south and downhill. Contour-following terraces step down the slope in ranks of dull red clay tile and grow older as they descend: rendered council cottage pairs in groups of four on the high ground, bay-fronted semis with hipped roofs and pebbledash upper storeys on the middle slopes, soot-darkened brick terraces lowest near the work, one short cul-de-sac of small thin-brick 1980s houses on the last plot. Party-wall chimney stacks with clay pots, a television aerial on every stack, one round satellite dish on a gable end. Stone retaining walls and flights of steps between streets. A slate-roofed chapel and a railed school yard mid-slope. Beyond the last roofs and 40 m below, the grey water of the harbour basin, dock cranes in silhouette, a tall brick works chimney further right. Slate-grey overcast sky. BOTTOM: camera at 1.6 m on the steep lower length of Chapel Road, gradient 1 in 9, looking uphill along a terrace of council cottages, chapel gate 60 m up. ONE ROW UNDER TWO MAINTENANCE REGIMES, house by house: the near house, bought from the council, has a new hardwood door with a sunburst glass panel, a brick porch added to the front, white plastic casement windows, stone cladding across the ground floor and a front garden paved over with a mass-market saloon on it; its neighbour, still rented, keeps the council's plain painted door, painted timber windows, a low chain-link fence and a clipped privet hedge. Party walls step up in half-storey jumps as the ground climbs and the end house sits on an underbuild, a cellar at one end and a garage at the other. Kerb and pavement run unbroken uphill, the pavement stepped with a steel handrail. Galvanised steel dustbins with lids against the wall by a side door, a wire crate of glass milk bottles on a doorstep, a concrete coal bunker in the side passage, sheets on a wire washing line in the back yard seen through the passage, a thread of coal smoke from one chimney, a steel lamp column. Flat overcast light after rain, wet tarmac, damp render, soot streaks below the gutters, moss in the kerb joints. Three nonidentifiable people in ordinary British clothes of 1990, one in a black donkey jacket with leather shoulder panels walking uphill. EXACTLY THREE PIECES OF LETTERING IN THE WHOLE SHEET: the title FAIRVIEW, the small subtitle CONCEPT PROPOSAL, and a pressed metal street nameplate on a garden wall reading CHAPEL ROAD in black capitals on white; each crisp and correctly spelled, every other surface plain unlettered render, brick, paint and glass. Two small rows along the bottom of the sheet: an upper row of four flat material swatches, light warm grey pebbledash, dull red clay roof tile, dark green privet, grey-brown coursed retaining stone; below it three objects against the paper border, a wire crate of glass milk bottles, a low timber garden gate, a leather school satchel. Both rows plain and unlabelled. Photoreal throughout, everything period-correct for 1990. A proposal drawn for review., invented fictional shop name only, no real company names, no real brand logos, no trade marks, no real person, no recognisable faces, no celebrity likeness
